chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nadr ibn Ishaq, from Anbasa ibn Sa'id, raised the hadith to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:
Frequent combing of the head removes the illness (fever), brings the livelihood, and increases in copulation.

key_terms.تَسْرِيح: Combing or grooming (specifically of the hair/head)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of combing the hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual and physical benefits of grooming, linking the act of combing hair to the removal of 'wabā’ (often interpreted as fever or epidemic plagues), the attraction of rizq (sustenance), and increased sexual vitality. This reflects the Shia tradition of viewing mundane acts of self-care as means of divine blessing when performed with mindfulness, connecting physical hygiene to spiritual and material well-being.
